title: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Amendment (Local Industry Preference) Bill 2026
short_title: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Amendment (Local Industry Preference) Bill 2026

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the bill text as introduced; not the record
sentences: The bill would change Commonwealth procurement law to require rules favouring domestic manufacturing in specified projects and add an objective supporting Australian industry and jobs.
It would require procurement rules to give domestic manufacturers opportunities for earlier consideration and set a minimum domestic manufacturing share for goods used in specified projects.
The requirements would include limited exemptions with transparency, and the whole bill would commence on the day following Royal Assent under its commencement table.
changes: At least 30% of the total goods value in specified projects would have to comprise domestically manufactured products.
Domestic manufacturers would receive opportunities for consideration before manufacturers from outside Australia when tendering for specified projects.
The rules would have to provide limited, transparent exemptions from both requirements.
summary.affected: Domestic and non-domestic manufacturers tendering for specified Commonwealth projects are affected.

speeches.speaker: Dai Le
speeches.brief: Moved the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Amendment (Local Industry Preference) Bill 2026, proposing that Commonwealth procurement support Australian industry and local jobs by prioritising domestic manufacturers for specified projects; the bill was seconded, and debate was adjourned.
